title: Brand pack (brand.json)
description: A brand as data (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §7): its palette, type by reference, logos and their build, motif, look, motion law, voice, sound palette, truth, grounding ids, the generator-uploads decision and its four approved references. Every engine reads brand.json as it is, so it is the one source of truth; files beside it that repeat part of it (motion.json, MOTION.md, onboarding/truth/TRUTH.md) are written from it by `slate brand onboard`. Keys starting with x_ are free for extensions; keys starting with _ are added at runtime and never saved.

name.description: The pack's folder name: how films and commands name the brand.

display_name.description: The brand as it's written and said.

about.description: What the brand is, in a sentence or two.

contrast_pairs.description: Every text colour pair the brand uses, by token or role: body text needs 4.5:1, large text 3:1.

motif.description: An optional brand mark made of parts (the kit's motif rig): parts, shape, corner, part_size, ring, groups, mark_ratio, orient, curves, and gestures (meaning → gesture kinds). file/path may point at the mark's SVG.

allow_generator_uploads.description: May brand material (logos, UI frames, references) be uploaded to generators? Only when the brand owner allows it; false by default.

ownership.description: Whose brand this is. own: the owner's own brand (the owner may rule on claims). client: a brand the owner doesn't own (a company, a client): its claim authority is a named person at that organisation. neutral: Slate's own demo and template. company_material: true keeps the pack on this Mac only (never in a repo with a remote) and means its source code is read in place, never copied.

palette.description: Colour tokens, flat or nested ("gray": {"50": "#…"}), as #RRGGBB (or any CSS colour; onboarding writes hex). roles names the kit's roles (page, surface, ink, ink2, ink3, hairline, accent, accentInk, softAccent, inverse, inverseDeep, line) by token or colour; tones gives ok, warn and risk as {dot} or {bg, ink, dot}.

fg.description: the text colour: a token, a role or a colour

role.description: body text needs 4.5:1, large text (≥ 24 px, or 18.7 px bold, at 1080 lines) 3:1

font_source.description: Fonts by reference only, never font files: installed (a font installed on the machine, used in place), google (Google Fonts, through @remotion/google-fonts), or a type service's kit (its stylesheet URL).

role.description: sans, display, serif, mono, or a role the brand names

licence.description: the licence it's used under (required for every family)

postscript.description: the PostScript name of this role's face, which After Effects sets fonts by

scale.description: optional overrides of the kit's text roles (hero, h1, body, …) as fractions of the frame's short side, or px with reference

file.description: the SVG, relative to the pack

svg.description: the SVG inline (the engine inlines file/path itself)

build.description: the logo build: guides (edges|none|{h, v}), vertices (corners|all|none), order, keystone, keystone_from, outline, impact, timing {construct, outline, fill, stagger, drop, out} in seconds or duration tokens

on.description: the background it's drawn for (a token or role)

marks.description: ® ™ and the like, per the guidelines

colourways.description: the mark in each colourway a film needs (ink and white at least): {ink|white|mono: the name of another logo in this pack, or an SVG relative to the pack}; the kit's LogoBuild and LogoSting draw the one for their ground, so builders never recolour a mark

grounded_in.description: the brand kit it was grounded in (elevenlabs:<id>, higgsfield:<id> or pack: the pack's own tokens and references)

id.description: the look from the looks library (flat, paper-2.5d, editorial, blueprint, an AE look) or the brand's own

references.description: reference films and frames the look draws on: {file, what, note}

ease.description: A named ease: [x1, y1, x2, y2], "cubic-bezier(…)", "linear", "sine", or {bezier | kind (linear, sine, spring0) and stiffness} with lineage (where it comes from), job, duration_s, peak (its highest point, above 1 when it overshoots).

motion.description: The brand's motion law. eases: named eases with lineage; durations: the duration scale ({token: seconds}); staggers: units ({unit: seconds} or {frames, at_fps}); stagger_cap: {seconds, fraction}; exit_factor; roles: which ease does each job (entrance, move, state, exit, relayout); overshoot: the policy ({allowed, max, where}); signature: the brand motif's signature motion; linear_props, loops, rigs, banned: the law's other rules; extra_curves and speed_limits: what `slate qa motion` allows beyond Slate's defaults.

durations.description: null (or left out) lets the kit's neutral scale stand in until onboarding writes one

extra_curves.description: The generic curves `slate qa motion` lets any move use besides the brand's named eases (by default only a rig part may use sway, land or spring0, and a carry even): sway ((1 - cos pi u)/2), land (cubic-bezier(0.25, 0, 0.25, 1)), spring0 (the kit's zero-bounce spring), even (the even travel profile). A brand ease of the same name always wins.

speed_limits.description: The brand's own speed and acceleration limits per motion class, replacing Slate's defaults (rig 30 px/frame and 8 px/frame squared, ui 60 and 16, carry 170 and 45, at a 1080 px short side): {rig|ui|carry: {speed, accel}} as fractions of the frame's short side, or as px with the short_side they were measured on ({speed: 30, accel: 8, short_side: 1080}). A whip has no limit of its own: a person judges it.

voice.description: The brand's voice profile (schemas/voice_profile.schema.json is the full contract; the voice module validates it): provider, source, voice_id, model, settings, seed, lexicon (brand words Whisper must hear in full), tag policy, pacing, fit and targets.

sound.description: The brand's sound palette. key, tempo (bpm or [lo, hi]), materials (what the effects are made of; the score never plays them), banned_timbres, instrumentation, motif ({instrument, …}: the character's own sound), palette (overrides of the starting palette, key by key: levels, kinds, rules), reference_levels (measured against the voice on the approved sound reference, LU per stem).

id.description: a short code a claim cites

pin.description: a commit, a date or a hash: what exactly was read

read.description: company code is always read in place

sources.description: the sources of truth, pinned; the product's own code first

claim_authority.description: the named person who rules on claims for this brand; for a brand the owner doesn't own, a person at that organisation

forms.description: its inflections: a banned "verified" is also "verifies", "verifying", "verification"

instead.description: the approved substitute a failure names ("trusted")

anyOf.description: a banned word with its forms and its substitute; every gate matches every form

self_commentary.description: false: graphics never caption themselves ("Illustration", "Example"), and the script and banned-words gates ban those captions on screen; true (the default) allows them

never_claim.description: what the film never says or shows: owner rulings, things not built, retracted words

sample_data.description: the one set of sample numbers films show (always labelled as sample data)

rulings.description: conflicts and the authority's rulings: {question, ruling, by, at, source}

grounding.description: Brand-kit ids that ground generations in the brand: ElevenLabs (Flows) and Higgsfield. uploads_allowed mirrors allow_generator_uploads (the generate stage reads it); if the two disagree the answer is no.

file.description: the approved file, relative to the pack (or absolute)

references.description: The four onboarding references, each null until a person approves it with `slate brand approve`.
